To: support@clockpoint.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: kevin.mutua@tausifreight.example
Subject: Re: [CP-48213] Overtime coding issue on night shifts

Dear Faith,

Please find the details for ticket CP-48213 below. I have copied Kevin Mutua, our payroll officer, who will test any fix or workaround you suggest.

1. Terminal model and firmware
The four BX-300 terminals at Embakasi auto-updated from firmware 4.1.8 to 4.2.1 on the night of 27 October. Our two Mombasa Road terminals remain on 4.1.8 because they were offline that week; the day shift there is unaffected.

2. Shift template
The affected staff use NIGHT-8, scheduled from 22:00 to 06:00.

3. Example
Staff ID T-0417 clocked in at 21:54 on 30 October and out at 06:07 on 31 October. All times are local Nairobi time.

The export showed:
- 30 October: 2.1 hours REG
- 31 October: 6.1 hours OT15

Expected: 8.0 hours REG plus 0.2 hours OT15. Payroll rounds durations to the nearest tenth of an hour, so the total of 8 hours 13 minutes becomes 8.2 hours. Only the 13 minutes outside the scheduled shift should be coded OT15.

4. Export profile
Payroll CSV v2.

5. When first noticed
Kevin first noticed the problem on 5 November while reviewing draft October overtime. The incorrect splitting and after-midnight OT15 coding appear to date from around 28 October, immediately after the update.

This affects 38 night-shift staff and overstated draft overtime by approximately KES 212,000. Kevin held the overtime lines and corrected them manually using raw punches, but this is not sustainable.

The 4.2.1 release notes promised improved midnight rollover handling; our experience has been the opposite. We need a fix or clear workaround before payroll cut-off on 20 November. Please confirm your next steps and expected timing.

Can Brian Ochieng, our IT colleague who manages the terminals, safely roll Embakasi back to 4.1.8 without losing punch data? Please confirm any backup requirements and rollback precautions before he proceeds.

Regards,
Njeri Mwangi
HR Manager
Tausi Freight
